## C Clean-only stage 2

Scope: validate, 1,980 frames; confidence, norm and random; clean condition only; no loss sweep. E, L and full F come from existing P1 products at matched frames.

Forwards per frame: **10 masked** (confidence, norm, 8 random, clean only) plus 2 shared = 12; the C-1 identity control is not included.

At the stage-1 measured cost of 75.6 ms per condition and 0.122 s fixed per frame: **0.88 s/frame → 0.5 GPU-hours** on 1,980 frames (0.5 with the identity control).

**Not this number:** the full damaged sweep at the same n2 costs 27.5 GPU-hours. the full damaged sweep at the same n2 costs this much and is NOT the cost of the clean-only plan; the two must not be quoted for each other.

**Cell coverage.** six of the seven locked cells have p_cw exactly 0, so the clean forward IS their value; the 8 dB cell needs the p = 0.001 node, which a clean-only run does not produce and would have to substitute with the clean value. Substitution error measured in stage 1: sparse_F_confidence 0.00005, sparse_F_norm 0.00000, sparse_F_random_mean 0.00006.

**Direction of bias:**

* stage-1 timing included CUDA warm-up and a GPU shared with a desktop session -> the per-condition figure is probably HIGH.
* stage 1 read every 33rd frame; a full run reads frames consecutively, so caching may make data loading cheaper -> the estimate may be HIGH on that count too.
* against both: a full run holds 1,980 frames of results in memory and writes a larger file, which stage 1 did not exercise -> the estimate may be LOW on that count.
* no per-frame cost was measured on a machine free of other load.
